methodological_rigor.justification: SPRINKLE (NCT05309668) is a phase I/II open-label PK bridging study in 36 children age 1-7 years across three cohorts (GC1 n=15, GC2 n=17, JC n=4), with a physiologically based PK-predicted 25 mg/m2 BID dose-finding phase in groups of three, and a prespecified primary PK endpoint using the FDA 60-140% acceptance range relative to the SPRINT capsule AUC geometric mean of 2,009 h*ng/mL. Power calculations (≥90% for each GC) assumed gCV% 30% and ±5% exposure difference, with the sample size re-evaluated against observed gCV%. Noncompartmental PK analysis via Phoenix WinNonlin per AstraZeneca standards is appropriate. Main limitations include small JC cohort (n=4 vs planned 6), single-arm design, short follow-up at DCO1 (some patients with <3 half-lives of PK coverage per authors' own caveat), and no efficacy endpoint at this interim report.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Single-arm phase I/II case-series-style PK bridging study (Oxford level 4). Clinical relevance is high: the granule formulation was approved by the FDA on September 10, 2025 on the basis of this study, extending selumetinib access to pediatric NF1-PN patients age ≥1 year who cannot swallow capsules, a clinically important vulnerable pediatric oncology-adjacent population. Efficacy is extrapolated from the SPRINT capsule study via PK bridging, which is a regulatory-acceptable pediatric development strategy but is not a direct efficacy demonstration in this trial.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript provides trial registration (NCT05309668), a detailed study design figure (Fig 1), participant disposition (39 screened, 36 dosed), demographics (Table 1), prespecified PK analysis set definitions, NCI-CTCAE v5 AE grading, sample size justification with FDA Guidance citation, and a clear extrapolation plan. Several numerical details (AEs of special interest, BSA subgroup PK, JC details, N-desmethyl parameters, palatability) are deferred to the Data Supplement. No explicit data/code availability statement is visible in the main text. TRIPOD is not applicable; CONSORT is appropriate for an interventional single-arm trial and the manuscript largely adheres to it.

novelty_literature.justification: Selumetinib is already approved for NF1-PN in pediatric patients age ≥2 or ≥3 years (SPRINT). The novel contribution is a granule formulation enabling administration in children age ≥1 year who cannot swallow capsules, with PK equivalence demonstrated per FDA bridging criteria, and directly supporting the September 2025 FDA approval. This is a meaningful extension of a known therapy to a younger vulnerable population rather than a first-in-class drug, but the regulatory and clinical implications for the youngest NF1-PN patients are substantive.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well structured with clear sections on PK (single dose, multiple dose, BSA and age effects, JC, metabolite), safety, and palatability. Tables and figures present geometric means with 95% CIs against the SPRINT benchmark. The discussion transparently notes that some single-dose PK estimates cover <3 half-lives and that DCO1 does not assess efficacy (deferred to DCO2 after 25 cycles). Precise, regulatory-quality language.

key_strengths: Prespecified FDA-aligned 60-140% PK acceptance range against SPRINT capsule exposure was met in both Global Cohorts (AUC0-12 geometric means 1,902 and 1,699 h*ng/mL)
Physiologically based PK-predicted dose-finding process confirmed 25 mg/m2 BID in children age 1-7 years
Manageable safety profile consistent with the capsule formulation with no grade ≥4 AEs, no discontinuations, and high treatment compliance (median 100%, mean 99.2%)
Regulatory impact: directly supported the September 2025 FDA approval of selumetinib granules for pediatric patients age ≥1 year
Palatability assessment showed improvement from cycle 1 to cycle 7 with 82.4% of doses swallowed without problems
key_concerns: Small Japan Cohort (n=4 vs planned 6) limits PK comparability inference for this population
Single-arm design with efficacy extrapolated from SPRINT rather than directly measured at DCO1
Short follow-up at DCO1 with some single-dose PK estimates covering <3 half-lives
No explicit data/code availability statement in the main text; heavy supplement dependency
Incremental novelty as a formulation bridging study of an already-approved drug
chief_reviewer.rationale: A rigorously conducted FDA-aligned PK bridging study in a vulnerable pediatric rare-disease population that directly supported regulatory approval; suitable for a top-tier clinical journal with minor revisions.
